$comment: Path → guard-tests → rules-doc map consumed by .claude/hooks/path-guard.mjs on every Write/Edit. Globs use Node's path.matchesGlob against repo-relative paths. Keep each domain's tests FAST (scan-style guards, pure-function suites) — they run on every edit that matches. tests/path-guard-map.test.ts validates this file: every glob must match a real file, every test and rules doc must exist, and every docs/claude/rules/*.md must be routed by at least one domain.

domains.name: auth-and-url-safety
domains.note: Session JWT only — never re-add unsigned identity sources. See CLAUDE.md "Auth — session JWT only".

domains.name: client-scripts
domains.note: Bundled <script> blocks run ONCE per session under the ClientRouter: init on astro:page-load (never DOMContentLoaded), re-read elements inside init(), replace document/window listeners rather than stacking them. See docs/claude/insights/domains/frontend.md "Astro and ClientRouter".

domains.name: clientrouter-pages
domains.note: These pages have each shipped a 'goes dead after in-site navigation' bug: init must re-run on astro:page-load, and module-level state must not capture the previous page's DOM.

domains.name: contracts-eligibility
domains.note: The contract-declaration window is derived, not stored: eligibility is reconstructed by PARSING MFL's transaction strings, so a shape this parser reads wrong is indistinguishable downstream from a player who was never acquired. parseTransactions() discards any acquisition that yielded no added ids, and rosters.astro then renders the years as plain text with no "Declare Contract" action — a silent no-op, never an error. That shipped: the add-only BBID claim ("16778,|500000|", a winning claim with nothing cut) was asserted against a hand-written "16778,|500000|," that MFL has never emitted, so the suite passed while every drop-free waiver claim in the league went undeclarable. Assert transaction parsing against tests/fixtures/mfl-transaction-strings.json — real recorded shapes — and keep it in parity with scripts/lib/roster-move-parse.mjs, which parses the same MFL field for Schefter. Freshness is part of correctness here for the same reason: the committed transactions feed is bundled at BUILD time, so mfl-transactions-cache.ts layers the last few days live over it — a page that reads only the static feed cannot see a claim inside its own 24-hour window. The write side has its own trap: an MFL cookie secret fails by being PRESENT AND EXPIRED, so a login gated behind "no cookie set" never runs — apply-pending-contracts.mjs carried that ordering until 2026-09-15 and silently stopped delivering approved declarations when the cookie died. Prefer the login; keep the cookie as the fallback. The parity test is only as strong as its corpus: tests/fixtures/mfl-transaction-strings.json held ONE league's ONE season (10 of the 60 shapes that exist) and stayed green for months while the two parsers disagreed on three shapes worth 286 rows — all of them absent from it. Re-record with scripts/record-transaction-shapes.mjs (offline, reads the committed feeds for every league and season); widen it, never trim it to make a test pass. Two shapes have no comma to key on and are decided by the row's TYPE, not its string: a two-segment "8925|625000" is an auction PRICE where "11957,|9122," is a cut list, so parseTransactionString takes the type. And "0000" in a pre-2017 drop segment is MFL's NOTHING-CUT sentinel, not a player — returned as an id it reaches describePlayer() and publishes the prose "Player 0000".

domains.name: dev-tooling
domains.note: These back the /ratchet, /rebase, /new-page, /new-cron, /guard-test and /rollover-check skills and the sibling-drift, guard-gap and fixture-recorder agents; their tests are the contract those skills rely on.

domains.name: free-agents
domains.note: The ⋮ menu sits right after the Player column (it was nine columns off-screen on a phone, #974) and its header carries the league's own verb; the acquisition itself lives in PlayerDetailsModal, so it reaches every page the modal does — which means WaiverClaimModal is mounted by that modal and by no page, the offer is a SESSION verdict from /api/claim-context (both leagues have a franchise 0001), and the form must survive landing before or after the context does. The waiver priority dialog opens on the synced order and time-boxes the live read; the page's signed-in verdict is computed ONCE (franchiseIdForLeague) and read back off #watch-list-bridge[data-signed-in], never a second copy. The Auction view is a LIVE board (Place Bid deep links, a 60s poll, a 36h clock), so it belongs to resolveAuctionWindow and not to `hasAuctionData` — the auction RESULTS feed keeps its rows all year, which left the board on the page in September. See docs/claude/insights/features/waiver-claims.md and watch-list.md.

domains.name: front-office-hub
domains.note: ONE panel serves both leagues (FrontOfficePanel.astro) and both routes are thin wrappers that must stay under 75 lines. Sections are gated on registry features and data presence, never on a league slug (the claim verb is the one documented exception). roster-analytics.ts declares no cap formula of its own. The AFL keeper board is owner-PRIVATE, not merely un-actionable — /api/afl-keepers enforces owner-only read. NFL/College stacks render for the SELECTED team only (16 teams of them measured 1.45 MB raw / 133 KB gzipped). See docs/plans/front-office-hub.md. A what-if toggle NEVER reaches the network: scenarios are scratch, and filing is the separate act of pressing Extend/Tag/Cut, which clears that player from the scenario so the projection cannot double-count it. Scenario storage goes through scopedLocalKey because both leagues have a franchise 0001.

domains.name: github-workflows
domains.note: No new vars.* feature gates (comment out cron: to disable a job; gate with a const in the script); league ids/hosts come from the registry; a weekly job needs isSeasonWindowOpen, not "the feeds have a completed week". Dependencies install ONLY via `uses: ./.github/actions/setup` — never npm (it ignores pnpm-lock.yaml and re-resolves peers, which killed five crons for four days), and never a raw pnpm/action-setup (it installs nothing). The pnpm version lives only in package.json#packageManager. A workflow MAY skip the install, but only while every `node scripts/…` it runs is dependency-free all the way down — an empty node_modules fails silently (dynamic import in a try/catch → exit 0, green check). See CLAUDE.md "Feature flags — code, not GitHub Actions variables" and docs/claude/rules/storage-and-build.md § "CI installs with pnpm, never npm". GitHub does NOT deliver a high-frequency schedule on this repo (measured: 5-8 runs/day against the 288 that */5 asks for, since 2026-08-27) — the PRIMARY trigger for the roster sync is the Vercel cron in vercel.json, whose bridge route must stay CRON_SECRET-gated and whose cadence is a Vercel BUILD SPEND decision, since every sync commit to main is a production build. See docs/claude/rules/storage-and-build.md § "GitHub’s `schedule` is not a cadence".

domains.name: mfl-live-shell
domains.note: MFL Live's shell is a bar with two things in it (brand, hamburger) and one drawer behind the hamburger — every destination, the theme control and sign in/out live in MflAppMenu, at every width. Two of that drawer's declarations are FIXES, not style, and both were measured in a browser: `visibility 200ms ease` interpolates discretely and stays hidden for the first instant of the open transition, so .focus() is a silent no-op and the drawer opens with focus stranded on the hamburger, one Tab from the page behind it (hence `visibility 0s linear` with the delay on CLOSE only); and content-box makes the panel 100dvh PLUS the safe-area insets on a notched phone, putting Sign out below the fold with nothing to scroll. See src/components/shared/mfl-live/MflAppMenu.astro.

domains.name: error-pages
domains.note: Astro finds its error page by the EXACT route `/500`. Delete src/pages/500.astro and the lookup falls through to `[...path].astro`, which pins 404 — so every SSR crash on the site renders as a missing page, which is how a P0 outage got triaged as a deleted route on 2026-09-08. Serving a 404 deliberately? Rewrite to a path no route claims, never to `/404` — that page sets no status, so it answers 200 and stays indexed.

domains.name: mfl-weekly-results
domains.note: MFL omits `matchup` on a week it has not paired up and lists the franchises on weeklyResults instead — array-wrapping that undefined 404'd the roster page. Prove every optional MFL node truthy before making a list of it. And the nflSchedule export goes CURRENT-WEEK-ONLY once the season opens unless you ask for W=ALL, so a week with no schedule loaded is UNKNOWN, never a bye — that conflation stamped BYE on all 17 weeks and hid every player's real points. And weeklyResults lists a franchise's ACTIVE LINEUP only, so a free agent, a practice-squad player and an IR player have NO row in it — keying the modal's Season Results payload off that feed alone hid the table for all three. `playerScores&W=<n>` (playerScores-by-week.json) is the full-pool fallback; it fills points and NFL matchup context only, never a roster or a starter status. A week's roster is a LIST: the AFL holds the same player in both conferences.

domains.name: nav-and-footer
domains.note: Two independent link registries, and "the footer" names both. nav-config.json's `footerLinks` is the nav DRAWER's bottom strip (one link, "Back to MFL"); the site footer deck is footer-config.ts, which lists page-directory IDS rather than paths. A page can sit in one, the other, or both — so a link removed from the nav is still reachable, and `routeEquivalence` (keyed by path, unrelated to the drawer) is what keeps the league toggle crossing between the two leagues' copies. The trap is guard COVERAGE, not the link: TheLeague's bare paths are clean URLs rewritten at runtime, so those pages must never be prerendered — and nav-drawer-links.test.ts only asserts that for pages listed in nav-config.json. Tidying a duplicate nav entry away therefore silently takes the page's prerender guard with it (this happened to /owners in Sept 2026), which is why footer-links.test.ts now asserts the same rule over its own link set.

domains.name: nfl-week-starts
domains.note: Anything asking when an NFL week starts reads src/utils/nfl-week-starts.mjs. Never re-derive kickoff from Labor Day and never hardcode a Week 1 Thursday — 2026 opened on a WEDNESDAY. Refresh the data with `node scripts/fetch-nfl-week-starts.mjs`.

domains.name: owners-poll
domains.note: The poll's chat budget is TWO posts a week (the column, with the ballot invite folded in, and the reveal) and the nag is push-only. Neither is SENT here any more: generate-pecking-order.mjs queues them and scripts/schefter-announce-pending.mjs delivers after the commit step. Neither lane PROBES a URL first — /pecking-order answers 200 every week of the season, and the per-issue permalink 500s in production today (docs/claude/followups/2026-09-17-pecking-order-permalink-500.md) — so queueing alone is what keeps the announcement behind the commit.

domains.name: page-directory-and-whats-new
domains.note: See CLAUDE.md "Changelog — one article a week, everything else stages". Everything user-facing STAGES; the Monday rollup publishes one article per league. A staged summary is one line (200 visible chars) because it renders as a bullet — depth belongs in a /guides page the line links to. Guide screenshots live in public/assets/guides/, never the changelog's directory. `both` means the full-management leagues only (registry `bestBall` flag), and both the rollup and the data test must route through leaguesForStagedChange(). And a link inside a description LIST item must stay reachable from whats-new-links.ts#htmlFragments: a fragment the guards cannot see is league-prefixed by the renderer anyway and ships pointing at the wrong league.

domains.name: page-forks
domains.note: A route under two league directories is a sibling: build a shared component, not a second page. See CLAUDE.md "Second league's copy of a page".

domains.name: player-acquisition
domains.note: The player card offers exactly one acquisition per player, decided by the SERVER: free agent -> Claim/Bid, held by a rival in the viewer's scope -> Trade for him, on the viewer's own roster -> neither. The scope is conference-aware (the AFL rosters the same player once per conference), and the two Trade Builders take different query params. Never gate the trade affordance on `canClaim` — that goes false for the whole auction season.

domains.name: rankings
domains.note: Rankings are per-league; rankings-scope.ts owns every storage key. See CLAUDE.md "Rankings are per-league".

domains.name: rosters-page
domains.note: Run `node scripts/roster-parity-check.mjs` before AND after editing — it is the only test of this 12k-line page's hydrated output.

domains.name: schefter-columns
domains.note: A column on a weekly cron is NOT breaking news: tier:'breaking' hands the post the homepage at P0 for 48h (selectBreakingStory → resolveHeroState), and three weekly columns at that tier preempted the regular-season daily rotation ~4 days in 7. Every article type must also export the full pipeline interface and declare relatedLinks. See tests/weekly-column-hero-claim.test.ts. The workflow is in this domain deliberately: the guard derives the weekly set from its cron→type map, so an edit there must re-run the guard. Dedup for a once-per-season id must read the season ARCHIVE, not just the live feed: the weekly archiver rotating the original out is what re-posted the 2026 schedule-release column to GroupMe six days into the season. isDuplicate and appendToFeed share that check and fail closed on an unreadable shard, and --week does not waive the season guard for a type whose id ignores the week. A roster-move `transaction` string is POSITIONAL and its add side carries a TRAILING COMMA, so it goes through parseRosterMove (scripts/lib/roster-move-parse.mjs) and never an ad-hoc split: splitting on the pipe and taking index 0 yields "16171,", a key no player map holds, which published a whole waiver column naming "Player 16171" instead of Kendre Miller and silently nulled its composite hero; and a `.filter(Boolean)` before indexing erases the empty add segment that marks a pure DROP ("|15749,"), crediting a team with a free pickup of the player it just cut. A BBID row whose bid the parser cannot read must never price as $0: a silent 0 is the same class of bug as the placeholder name. An announcement is published in TWO steps: the generator ENQUEUES it (scripts/lib/announce-queue.mjs) and scripts/schefter-announce-pending.mjs sends it after the commit step, once the permalink answers 200 — posting from the generator advertises a permalink the deploy has not shipped yet, and news/[id].astro answers that with a redirect to the Schefter index.

domains.name: staging-and-deploy-environment
domains.note: The staging sites share PRODUCTION'S database and PRODUCTION'S secrets. Reads and Redis writes are the accepted cost; the outbound half is not, because none of it can be undone — an MFL write mutates the real league, a push reaches real phones, a GroupMe post lands in the real chat, an issue lands in the real backlog. Every outbound path calls assertOutboundAllowed/outboundAllowed from src/utils/deploy-environment.ts immediately before the network call, never at the route layer (a dozen routes, and the one that forgot fails open). The predicate is the DEPLOYMENT (VERCEL_ENV), not the request host, so PR previews are covered too; isStagingHost is the separate host question, for the noindex header and the banner. Unknown fails OPEN so cron scripts and pnpm dev keep working. A blocked write must also REPORT itself: every MFL write's catch runs through describeMflFailure (src/utils/mfl-fetch.ts), which is why the writer utils and write routes are routed here — collapsed into the network-failure branch, a staging refusal reached owners as HTTP 502 "Could not reach MFL". See docs/plans/staging-release-process.md. Release-day blackout windows are mechanical (scripts/release-blackout.mjs, run by /promote): NFL game days in season, the Feb 14 and Labor Day rollovers, and the AFL draft — all evaluated in PT, because the league's clock is PT and a UTC-evaluated Sunday starts at 4pm Saturday Pacific.

domains.name: origin-check
domains.note: Astro's checkOrigin 403s a non-GET request with no content type (or a form-like one) unless Origin matches exactly, and some browsers omit Origin. Every browser POST/DELETE and sendBeacon sends Content-Type: application/json. See docs/claude/insights/features/visit-surface-tracking.md.

domains.name: watch-list
domains.note: MFL's myWatchList is owner-cookie-only and incremental; the Redis mirror is a read cache keyed by registry slug. See docs/claude/insights/features/watch-list.md.

domains.name: web-push-and-pwa
domains.note: Two AFL-only bugs, both invisible in a diff. A manifest whose `scope` is not `/` is DISCARDED on the league's apex domain (every league is served at the root there, and vercel.json 301s `/<slug>/*` away), taking the install and the app icon with it. And Android renders a notification `badge` from its ALPHA CHANNEL alone, so an opaque favicon becomes a solid white square — badges are the white-on-transparent `badge-96.png` stencils, regenerated by scripts/generate-notification-icons.mjs, never a favicon. Admin-only `ops` categories (a failed cron, drifted MFL settings) are gated on the RECIPIENT, not the league: sendPushToFranchise recomputes admin-ness from the franchise id, so a fan-out payload cannot address them to the whole league. And "does this owner have the app?" is NOT a question the device can answer: `display-mode: standalone` is false in the desktop browser of someone whose phone has had it installed for a month, and Chrome keeps firing `beforeinstallprompt` there because on that device it genuinely is installable — so the install banner is suppressed by an ACCOUNT record (src/utils/app-install-state.ts), never by a device-local dismissal alone. The banner is also a direct child of both homepages' two-column grid, so it must span every track or it takes a column and folds the page.

domains.name: year-rollover
domains.note: Two independent clocks (Feb 14 → getCurrentLeagueYear, Labor Day → getCurrentSeasonYear); the base year is ALWAYS calendarYear - 1. See CLAUDE.md "Year rollover — two independent clocks".

domains.name: top-players
domains.note: The leaderboard reads player-scores-weekly.json, NOT weekly-results-raw.json: the latter records a player's score only for weeks he sat on some roster, so the free-agent pool is structurally invisible in it (163 of 484 scorers in TheLeague's week 1 2026). Ownership is a LIST — the AFL rosters the same NFL player once per conference. The week range comes from each league's own league.json (TheLeague 1-17, the AFL 1-18), never a constant. Page and component globs join `paths` in the phases that create them.
